office-chair.definition: A chair designed for desk work, often with adjustable height and back support.
office-chair.exampleUsage: The office chair was adjusted to the desk height.

filing-cabinet.definition: A piece of furniture used to store documents in drawers.

cubicle.definition: A small office workspace separated from others by partitions.

standing-desk.definition: A desk high enough to be used while standing, sometimes adjustable between sitting and standing heights.
standing-desk.exampleUsage: The standing desk can be lowered for seated work.

conference-table.definition: A large table designed for people to sit around while holding a meeting.

whiteboard.definition: A smooth board for writing with markers that can be erased.

bulletin-board.definition: A board where notices and student work are displayed.

partition.definition: A divider separating areas within an office.

computer.definition: An electronic device that processes information and runs programs.
computer.exampleUsage: The computer processed the measurements and saved the results.

monitor.definition: A screen that displays information from a computer.
monitor.exampleUsage: The monitor displayed the file that the technician had opened.

keyboard.definition: A set of keys used to type text and control a computer.
keyboard.exampleUsage: She entered the sample number using the keyboard.

mouse.definition: A hand-operated electronic device that controls the coordinates of a cursor on your computer screen as you move it around on a pad.
mouse.exampleUsage: He used the mouse to move the pointer to the selected file.

printer.definition: A machine that puts digital text or images onto paper.
printer.exampleUsage: The printer produced a paper copy of the approved report.

scanner.definition: A device that turns a paper image or document into a digital file.
scanner.exampleUsage: The scanner converted the paper document into a digital image.

projector.definition: A device that displays images on a wall or screen.
projector.exampleUsage: The projector displayed the presentation on the wall.

shredder.definition: A device that shreds documents (usually in order to prevent the wrong people from reading them).
shredder.exampleUsage: The shredder cut the approved disposal papers into small pieces.

fax-machine.definition: A device that sends and receives copies of documents through a telephone or communications line.
fax-machine.exampleUsage: The office still has a fax machine for older workflows.

copier.definition: Apparatus that makes copies of typed, written or drawn material.

headset.definition: Headphones with a microphone for listening and speaking.

webcam.definition: A small camera that sends live video to a computer.

router.definition: (computer science) a device that forwards data packets between computer networks.
router.exampleUsage: The router directed traffic between the office network and another network.

server.definition: A computer that provides data or services to other computers.

usb-drive.definition: A small portable digital storage device that connects through a USB port.
usb-drive.exampleUsage: The report was copied to a USB drive.

external-hard-drive.definition: A separate storage device for keeping large amounts of data.
external-hard-drive.exampleUsage: She saved a separate copy of the files on an external hard drive.

docking-station.definition: A device that connects a laptop to several accessories at once.
docking-station.exampleUsage: The docking station connected the laptop to a monitor and peripherals.

phone-system.definition: Equipment and services used to connect and manage telephone calls, using traditional, digital, or internet-based technology.

video-conferencing.definition: Live sound and video connect people in separate places through networked devices with cameras and microphones.
video-conferencing.exampleUsage: The remote team used video conferencing for the weekly meeting.

reception.definition: The area where visitors are welcomed and given information.

lobby.definition: A large entrance or reception room or area.

break-room.definition: A room where employees can rest, eat, or take scheduled breaks.
break-room.exampleUsage: Employees ate lunch in the break room.

meeting-room.definition: A room reserved for group meetings, often located in an office, school, hotel, or community center.

corner-office.definition: An office located at a building corner, usually with windows on two sides.
corner-office.exampleUsage: The corner office has windows facing two streets.

open-floor-plan.definition: An office layout with few full-height walls, creating a large shared work area.
open-floor-plan.exampleUsage: The team works in an open floor plan.

mailroom.definition: A room or department where incoming and outgoing mail and parcels are sorted and handled.
mailroom.exampleUsage: Packages are collected from the mailroom.

storage-room.definition: A designated room for organizing and keeping supplies, materials, or equipment until they are needed.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.

dress-code.definition: An official rule sets out the clothing permitted in a particular environment, such as a school or workplace.

happy-hour.definition: A period when a bar offers alcoholic drinks for less than usual.

team-building.definition: Activities intended to improve communication, cooperation, and working relationships within a team.
team-building.exampleUsage: The department held a team-building workshop.

performance-review.definition: A formal assessment of a worker’s job during a defined period, usually led by a manager to help improve their work.

onboarding.definition: The process of introducing and integrating a new employee into an organization, role, and workplace systems.
onboarding.exampleUsage: The new employee completed onboarding during the first week.

remote-work.definition: Work performed away from a central workplace, often from home, using communication technology.
remote-work.exampleUsage: The company allows remote work for some roles.

flex-hours.definition: A work arrangement that lets employees vary their starting and finishing times within agreed limits.
flex-hours.exampleUsage: The policy allows flex hours for eligible staff.

open-door-policy.definition: A workplace policy encouraging employees to approach managers or leaders with questions or concerns.
open-door-policy.exampleUsage: The manager explained the team's open-door policy.

water-cooler.definition: A machine that cools water and provides it for people to drink.
water-cooler.exampleUsage: The visitor filled a cup at the water cooler.

office-party.definition: A social gathering organized for employees at or by a workplace.
office-party.exampleUsage: The office party included games and snacks.

desk.definition: A table or work surface used for reading, writing, or computer work.

bookshelf.definition: A shelf or set of shelves for keeping books.

laptop.definition: A portable computer with a built-in screen and keyboard.

kitchen.definition: A room or area where food is prepared.
